# Pogue Digital Solutions, LLC

> Pogue Digital Solutions is a veteran-owned digital strategy and AI systems consultancy in Conroe, Texas, founded by John M Pogue. It helps founder-led businesses and organizations organize their knowledge, clarify their brand voice, and build practical AI-assisted marketing and business systems, with a human approving the work.

## Key facts

- Legal name: Pogue Digital Solutions, LLC
- Founder: John M Pogue, Founder and Creative Strategist. Navy veteran and former Hospital Corpsman. M.S. in Digital Marketing, Full Sail University. B.A. in Visual Communication.
- Location: Conroe, Texas. Serves Greater Houston and clients nationwide.
- Status: Veteran-owned, founder-led small business
- Core offers: Brand Voice AI (an AI-assisted business operating system that captures a company's knowledge, voice, and standards), AI and automation, digital strategy, training and workshops, government and organizational services
- Method: The Compass Method (Purpose, Skill, Opportunity, Service, with Heart at the center)
- Government: SAM.gov registered. UEI Y6S7ZHLJH5V6, CAGE 219K1. Primary NAICS 541613.
- Book a call: https://calendly.com/poguedigitalsolutions/30min
- Email: john@poguedigitalsolutions.com
- LinkedIn: https://www.linkedin.com/in/johnpogue

## Blog

Each article opens with a short, direct answer to the question in its title.

- [What Should a Small Business Automate First?](https://poguedigitalsolutions.com/blog/what-should-a-small-business-automate-first): Automate the task you repeat most often that requires the least judgment. For most small businesses that is one of three things: answering the same inbound question, sending the same follow-up, or moving the same information from one place to another by hand. Pick one. Document how you do it today. Then, and only then, look at tools.
- [What Is Brand Voice AI?](https://poguedigitalsolutions.com/blog/what-is-brand-voice-ai): Brand Voice AI is an AI-assisted business operating system. It captures what a company knows, how it communicates, who it serves, and how it makes decisions, then organizes that into a foundation that people and AI tools can both work from. The result is consistency. Your website, your emails, your proposals, and your AI-drafted content all sound like the same business, and a human approves the work before it goes out.
- [How Do You Capture the Knowledge Inside a Founder's Head?](https://poguedigitalsolutions.com/blog/how-do-you-capture-the-knowledge-inside-a-founders-head): You do it through structured conversation, not a questionnaire, and you do it in rounds. A founder cannot sit down and write out everything they know, because most of what they know does not feel like knowledge to them. It feels like common sense. The job is to ask the questions that make the invisible visible, record the answers, organize them into categories a stranger could use, and then come back for a second pass once the founder sees what they missed.
- [AI Has a New Name in Washington. Laughable or Not, Learn It.](https://poguedigitalsolutions.com/blog/ai-has-a-new-name-in-washington): Federal agencies now call AI "super intelligence," and a new Super Intelligence Force led by Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton has 120 days to report on AI's risks and opportunities. The name change is mostly PR, but small business owners should learn the term, use both words for a while, and watch for the task force report around early February 2027.
- [Why I Named My AI Assistant Ms MoneyPenny](https://poguedigitalsolutions.com/blog/why-i-named-my-ai-assistant-ms-moneypenny): What a land tech in an oil and gas office taught John M Pogue about the job an AI assistant should do: organize, draft, guard the calendar, and never send without a yes.
- [A Starship Traded Its Library for a Ride Home](https://poguedigitalsolutions.com/blog/a-starship-traded-its-library-for-a-ride-home): A 1995 Star Trek: Voyager episode explains why your stories are the one thing AI cannot produce when anyone can publish a thousand posts a day.
- [The Builders Asked for Brakes. The Government Gave Three Answers.](https://poguedigitalsolutions.com/blog/the-builders-asked-for-brakes): AI companies asked to slow down. The government gave three answers at once. A Navy surgical count, film ratings, and the ESRB show what real oversight needs.
- [AI's "Wild West" Phase Needs a Regulator, Not a Waiver](https://poguedigitalsolutions.com/blog/ais-wild-west-phase-needs-a-regulator-not-a-waiver): AI labs want an antitrust waiver to coordinate on safety. Lessons from debt collection and Sarbanes-Oxley point to an independent public referee instead.
- [Siri AI Ships Monday.](https://poguedigitalsolutions.com/blog/siri-ai-ships-monday-apple-has-run-this-play-before): Apple is paying Google to power the new Siri while building its own replacement. The Motorola ROKR shows how this partnership may end, and what small businesses can learn.
- [Your best customer already bought.](https://poguedigitalsolutions.com/blog/your-best-customer-already-bought): Your past customers are your most valuable asset. Three ways a small business can sell them the next thing: the natural next purchase, a maintenance plan, and an introduction.
- [We Already Accepted the Machine. We Just Forgot We Did.](https://poguedigitalsolutions.com/blog/we-already-accepted-the-machine): In 1713 a boy rigged a steam engine to run its own valves. The same lesson applies to AI: automate the repetition and keep human judgment where it belongs.
- [AI Won't Take Your Job, But It Will Change Who Keeps It!](https://poguedigitalsolutions.com/blog/ai-wont-take-your-job-but-it-will-change-who-keeps-it): The professionals who keep their jobs will direct, challenge, evaluate, and multiply AI output. A human and AI workflow for starting strong and finishing strong.
- [What's Your Bottleneck? Can AI Be the Solution?](https://poguedigitalsolutions.com/blog/whats-your-bottleneck-can-ai-be-the-solution): Adding AI does not remove a bottleneck. It can help you reach it faster. Where AI work slows down before, during, and after, and how to open the flow.
- [Afraid AI Will Take Your Job? Here's How to Become Harder to Replace](https://poguedigitalsolutions.com/blog/afraid-ai-will-take-your-job): How to become harder to replace with AI: open big by defining the problem, let AI do the heavy lifting, and close big with human judgment and accountability.
- [AI Marketing Is Not a Funnel Anymore. It Is a Business Operating System.](https://poguedigitalsolutions.com/blog/ai-marketing-is-not-a-funnel-anymore): Customers do not fall through a funnel. Marketing in the AI era needs continuity across research, brand, offers, content, and approval: a business operating system.
- [Tell Me Your Origin Story](https://poguedigitalsolutions.com/blog/tell-me-your-origin-story): Marvel made superheroes human by showing their struggles. Your business has an origin story too, and telling it is how customers come to root for you.
- [Rebel Without a Claude: Stop Sounding Like Everyone Else's AI](https://poguedigitalsolutions.com/blog/rebel-without-a-claude): AI is making entrepreneurs sound alike. The fix is giving AI more of you: your stories, opinions, humor, and values, so it amplifies the identity you already have.
- [What Roger Corman Taught Me About Learning AI](https://poguedigitalsolutions.com/blog/what-roger-corman-taught-me-about-learning-ai): Three lessons from filmmaker Roger Corman that apply to learning AI: do the rough things first, plan but be ready to change, and open big and close big.
- [Don't Tell Me It Can't Be Done: Rethinking the LinkedIn Profile Ring](https://poguedigitalsolutions.com/blog/rethinking-the-linkedin-profile-ring): LinkedIn only offers an #OpenToWork ring. How John M Pogue turned that limitation into a custom profile badge, a branding workflow, and a Custom GPT.
- [How I Lost 3.5 Years of ChatGPT History in One App Update](https://poguedigitalsolutions.com/blog/how-i-lost-3-5-years-of-chatgpt-history): One ChatGPT app update wiped three and a half years of organized projects. Why you should export your AI history every 90 days, and the backup guide to do it.
- [Why I Won't Miss the AI Revolution](https://poguedigitalsolutions.com/blog/why-i-wont-miss-the-ai-revolution): John M Pogue watched the internet and smartphone revolutions from the sidelines. Why he is prepared for the AI revolution, and why this time he is in the game.
- [Why Isn't America a Perfect 100? A Veteran's Curiosity About Freedom Rankings](https://poguedigitalsolutions.com/blog/why-isnt-america-a-perfect-100): A veteran looks at why Freedom House scores the United States 81 out of 100, how freedom indexes define freedom, and what a homegrown scorecard might weigh.
- [The Future of Marketing Isn't Advertising. It's Shareable Experiences](https://poguedigitalsolutions.com/blog/the-future-of-marketing-is-shareable-experiences): People rarely share ads. They share experiences. How businesses design photo-worthy moments that turn customers into brand ambassadors and earned media.
- [Why Credit Cards Are a Terrible "Emergency Fund"](https://poguedigitalsolutions.com/blog/why-credit-cards-are-a-terrible-emergency-fund): Available credit is not savings. Card companies can cut limits or close accounts when you need them most. The Credit Avenger case for a real cash reserve.
- [What I'd Do With a $2,000 Tariff Refund (Credit Avenger Style)](https://poguedigitalsolutions.com/blog/what-id-do-with-a-2000-tariff-refund): The Credit Avenger plan for a $2,000 windfall: shore up the emergency fund, hit the debt snowball, kill a monthly payment, and invest in skills that pay.
